shots.say: Every Sunday, Maya opens her pantry and sees dinner nowhere. Six ingredients. No plan. Another takeaway.
Pantry Pal looks at the same six ingredients and sees the whole week. Watch what one click does.
Recipe apps hand you a shopping list. Pantry Pal never does. Nothing to buy is the whole point.
It starts with what is actually there. Chicken, rice, chickpeas, tomatoes, onions, one jar of garam masala.
One click. Six dinners, planned from what she already owns. Monday curry, Tuesday chickpea rice, Wednesday's remix.
Monday is chicken curry. Twenty-five minutes, one pan, the tomatoes and onions she already had.
The number that matters: six dinners, zero dollars extra. The pantry paid for the week already.
And one pot to wash. Every dinner cooks in the same pan, so the week ends cleaner than it started.
Wednesday is the remix. Yesterday's rice meets today's curry, and leftovers stop being a chore.
Tuesday's chickpea rice takes twenty minutes. The week never asks for more time than a weeknight has.
No model calls. No backend. The whole app is static pages served locally — the plan is the product.
Six dinners. Zero extra shopping. One pot to wash.
